note: Cross-process parity fixture for Drift's two glob engines: `matchesGlob` (packages/core/src/globs.ts) and `path_glob_matches` (crates/drift-engine/src/check_command.rs). They share no code across the CLI/engine process boundary, so this differential is the only thing holding them together. `selected` is the actual output of the Rust matcher over `globs` x `files`, in `files` order; it was generated, never hand-written. Both sides recompute it from scratch: crates/drift-engine/src/check_command.rs::glob_engine_parity_tests and packages/core/test/glob-parity.test.ts. A change to either matcher alone turns its own side red. There is deliberately no regeneration flag - if this goes red, decide which matcher is wrong from the semantics documented above `path_glob_matches`, and fix that matcher.
pattern_cases_note: Single-pattern rows for the semantics the proposer's glob set does not exercise, `matches` generated the same way. The `/api/users/*` rows are the one input on which the two engines were ever measured to disagree: `path_glob_matches` carried a widening that also matched the bare directory, and `matchesGlob` did not. The widening was real but belonged to phase5's route-path domain, so it moved to `phase5_scope_pattern_matches` and the general matcher is strict globstar on both sides now.
